item.title: "Informational Advisory: SonicOS Client DPI-SSL Trust of Compromised eMudhra Certificate Chain"
item.description:
""SonicWall has addressed an issue in SonicOS where appliances with Client DPI-SSL enabled continued to trust certificate chains issued by compromised eMudhra intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs) . Because the firewall’s local certificate store trusted the underlying root certificates, the firewall re-signed traffic from impacted servers with the local SonicWall DPI-SSL CA certificate, preventing client browsers from rejecting connections signed by the untrusted intermediate CAs. SonicWall has remediated this issue by removing the affected root certificates from the SonicOS certificate store and implementing blocking logic for the compromised intermediate certificate chain. SonicWall strongly recommends that customers upgrade to the latest release versions listed below to address and mitigate the associated risks. CVE: None Last updated: Nov. 10, 2026, 8:57 a.m.""

item.title: "November 2026 Security Update"
item.description:
""Ivanti releases standard security patches on the second Tuesday of every month. In today’s rapidly evolving technology and threat landscape, we believe responsible transparency should be a cornerstone of any product security program. AI is compressing the time-to-exploit , and Ivanti uses leading technologies to proactively find and fix issues––including integrating advanced LLMs into our Engineering and product security to enhance the capabilities of our teams and identify vulnerabilities that traditional tools have previously missed. Our philosophy is simple: discovering and communicating vulnerabilities and sharing that information with defenders is not an indication of weakness; rather it is evidence of rigorous scrutiny and a proactive vulnerability management program. By aggressively seeking to identify and address vulnerabilities, our aim is to get ahead of threat actors to ensure our customers can take the steps needed to protect their environments. Ivanti is disclosing vulnerabilities in Ivanti User Workspace Manager, Ivanti Sentry, Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile, Ivanti Cloud Services Application and Ivanti Endpoint Manager. It is important for customers to know: We have no evidence of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild. These vulnerabilities do not impact any other Ivanti solutions. More information on these vulnerabilities and detailed instructions on how to remediate the issues can be found in the Security Advisories: Ivanti User Workspace Manager Ivanti Sentry Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile Ivanti Cloud Services Application Ivanti Endpoint Manager How we are using AI in product security Ivanti continues to explore, test, and implement leading technologies and processes in every stage of our product development. Our security team has integrated multiple advanced LLM models into our product security processes. This has increased the capabilities of our Engineering and Product Security Red Teams to identify and fix vulnerabilities, especially those that are difficult to identify with traditional tooling, such as SAST and DAST. We have already successfully identified vulnerabilities which traditional tools missed, including some that we are disclosing today. As these tools are integrated further into our processes and refined, we expect an increase in vulnerability disclosures. We will continue to share transparently what we have found and resolved to ensure the security of our products. If you are not already following our Security Blog or subscribed to receive alerts for updates on the products you own through the Ivanti Innovators Hub, we highly recommend you do so. Importantly, we are committed to using AI responsibly in product security, including keeping a human in the loop to verify automated or agentic work. While this will result in an uptick in disclosures, we see this as a good thing, and an important part of ensuring our products keep pace with modern security requirements as they change. Our top priority is the security of our customers and believe the increase in identified, resolved, and transparently communicated vulnerabilities demonstrates that commitment. Our Support team is always available to help customers and partners should they have any questions. Cases can be logged via the Ivanti Innovators Hub (login credentials required). Want to stay up to date on Ivanti Security Advisories? Paste https://www.ivanti.com/blog/topics/security-advisory/rss into your preferred RSS reader / functionality in your email program.""

item.title: "SonicWall SonicOS Affected By Multiple Vulnerabilities"
item.description:
""1) CVE-2026-107155 - Permissive Cross-domain Policy Vulnerability A permissive cross-domain policy vulnerability has been identified in the SonicOS management interface, which in specific conditions could potentially enable a remote unauthenticated attacker to perform unauthorized operations. CVSS Score: 8.8 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains 2) CVE-2026-107154 - Session Validation Vulnerability A session validation vulnerability has been identified in the SonicOS management interface, which in specific conditions could potentially enable a remote unauthenticated attacker to perform unauthorized operations. CVSS Score: 8.8 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H CWE-291: Reliance on IP Address for Authentication 3) CVE-2026-82308 - Pre-authentication Heap Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in SSL-VPN A pre-authentication heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability has been identified in the SonicOS SSL-VPN service, which could potentially enable a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause an application level denial of service. CVSS Score: 7.5 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow 4) CVE-2026-19868 - SSLVPN Authentication Enforcement Vulnerability via Alternate Authentication Methods An authentication enforcement vulnerability in SonicOS SSLVPN service may allow a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls. Successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA). IMPORTANT: SonicWall PSIRT has investigated a report indicating potential exploitation of this vulnerability. Customers are strongly urged to upgrade to the latest release as soon as possible to mitigate the associated risks. NOTE: This vulnerability ONLY impacts the SonicOS SSLVPN interface or service if SAML is enabled for SSLVPN logins. CVSS Score: 7.1 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N CWE-308: Use of Single-factor Authentication 5) CVE-2026-77708 - Pre-authentication Stack Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in TACACS+ A pre-authentication stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability has been identified in the SonicOS TACACS+ authentication client, which in specific conditions could potentially enable a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause an application level denial of service. CVSS Score: 5.9 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H CWE-121: Stack-based Buffer Overflow 6) CVE-2026-77709 - Pre-authentication Heap Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in TACACS+ A pre-authentication heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability has been identified in the SonicOS TACACS+ authentication client, which in specific conditions could potentially enable a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause an application level denial of service. CVSS Score: 5.9 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow 7) CVE-2026-19703 - Weak Password Hashing A weak password hashing vulnerability has been identified on SonicOS virtual appliances, which in specific conditions could potentially enable an attacker with existing local access to disclose a platform credential. The credential provides access to a limited subset of platform settings. CVSS Score: 5.2 CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials CVE: CVE-2026-77708, CVE-2026-77709, CVE-2026-82308, CVE-2026-107154, CVE-2026-107155, CVE-2026-19703, CVE-2026-19868 Last updated: Nov. 9, 2026, 10:40 a.m.""
